newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu opposes U.S. plea to close tunnel - sources.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu opposes U.S. plea to close tunnel - sources.

text.p: The United States asked Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to close down the tunnel that re-ignited violence with Palestinians, but the Israeli leader seemed opposed, diplomatic sources said on Thursday.

The sources told Reuters that Netanyahu, in a telephone conversation with Secretary of State Warren Christopher, said closing the tunnel was not an option for political reasons and also because it would reward violence.
One source said Christopher had "suggested" to Netanyahu to shut the archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy places in Jerusalem.
The decision to open the tunnel by Israel's right-wing government unleashed gun battles and stone-throwing clashes that was the worst fighting since Palestinians set up their self-rule government.

The source said Netanyahu did not give Christopher a "specific response but the general feeling is that this is not something the government is able to do ... both for domestic reasons and also because it will be seen as a reward for violence."
Another source said he understood "Christopher told Netanyahu in no uncertain terms that dramatic measures must be taken to turn this situation back."
